clue.text: Cold massage breaking ship's surgeon's habit

indicators.note: something breaking into a thing splits it open and sits inside it

parts.note: SS is the abbreviation for steamship, the usual prefix to a ship's name
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
a rub is a massage

explanation.surface: A ship's doctor has an odd routine of chilly massages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habit' is clothing here, as a nun's habit is, not a routine; 'ship's' supplies the usual steamship abbreviation that wraps the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrubs are the plain loose clothes surgeons wear in the operating theatre, so they are a surgeon's garb.

clue.text: Married man hides crush

indicators.note: a thing that hides something keeps it tucked away inside itself

parts.note: a chap is a man
M is the standard abbreviation for married

explanation.surface: A married man keeps quiet about having a crush on someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crush' reads as an infatuation, but it is a verb: to chew or mash.
explanation.definitionFit: To champ is to munch or grind with the jaws, crushing food noisily between the teeth.

clue.text: Let go of handle and sue after collapsing

indicators.note: a structure that has collapsed lies in a jumbled heap, so the letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone drops the handle of a lawsuit after the case falls apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Unleashed means released or freed, like a dog let off its lead, which is the sense of let go.

clue.text: Perhaps Google Maps gave data for dynamic growth according to terms

indicators.note: terms are ends or limits, so taking the words according to their terms means using each one's final letter

parts.words: Maps gave data for dynamic growth
parts.note: the last letter of each of the six words

explanation.surface: A tech firm boasts that its mapping data drove rapid growth, by its own terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Google Maps' reads as one product name, but the definition stops at Google; the six words after it supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To google something is to look it up online, so it is an example of the verb meaning to look for.

clue.text: Criminal mastermind finally traps James Bond — overlooking very problematic plot point?

indicators.note: traps means holds something captive inside, so one part goes within another
finally points to the closing letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: final letter of the word

indicators.note: overlooking something means missing it out, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: Bond is agent 007, spoken as double-O seven
V is the usual abbreviation for very
final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A Bond villain captures 007, and the film forgets a glaring hole in its story.
explanation.walkthrough: Bond is reduced to his number written as letters, double-O SEVEN, which loses its V before going between L and D.
explanation.definitionFit: A loose end is an unresolved strand of a story, a detail left untied that troubles a careful viewer.

clue.text: Practise to get better — and hear why later when put to work

indicators.note: words put to work are reshaped for a new job, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to a trainee: keep practising and you will understand the reasons once you are on the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'and' look like a join, but it belongs to the letters being rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To learn the hard way is to improve through painful experience and mistakes rather than easy instruction.

clue.text: Count more than two huge icebergs originally at sea

indicators.note: something at sea is confused and adrift, so the letters are tossed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: originally points to the first letter, where the word begins

parts.note: first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sailor tallies more than two enormous icebergs out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: To outweigh is to matter more than something else, which is what counting for more than it means.

clue.text: Keen to have time in Ecuador on vacation

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside another
a place on vacation is vacated, emptied of its middle, so only its outer letters stay

parts.note: first and last letters of the country
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone is keen to spend some time in Ecuador on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On vacation' sounds like going away on a trip; here it empties the country's name of its middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Eager and keen are synonyms, both describing someone enthusiastic and impatient to do something.

clue.text: Direction from Gagarin — or the astronaut

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: runs across the end of the cosmonaut's name and the next words

explanation.surface: A space traveller like Yuri Gagarin gives a heading from orbit.
explanation.walkthrough: Yuri Gagarin was the Soviet cosmonaut who first orbited the Earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Northeast is a compass point, one of the bearings that indicate a direction of travel.

clue.text: Coming in considerably tense, entirely foolish person doesn't cope

indicators.note: coming in means entering, so one group of letters goes inside another

parts.note: far as in far better, meaning considerably
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
all means entirely, as in all alone
a sap is a fool

explanation.surface: Arriving in a very anxious state, a complete idiot cannot manage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like an adjective for the person's state, but it is the grammar term; 'coming in' places the fool's pieces inside the others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who falls apart breaks down emotionally, failing to cope with a situation.

clue.text: Blood on zip at the front

parts.note: go means energy or vim, as does zip
re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: Blood smeared on the zip at the front of a garment, as in a crime scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At the front' places the word for zip before the word for on.
explanation.definitionFit: Gore is blood shed from a wound, especially clotted blood in violent scenes.

clue.text: Item Banksy used, e.g. to screen publicity about name

indicators.note: to screen something is to shield it from view by surrounding it

parts.note: say means for example, like e.g.
PR stands for public relations, publicity
ca is short for circa, Latin for about
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A gallery note on the tools Banksy used, perhaps to hide from publicity his real name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' looks like a reversal signal but gives circa's abbreviation. Banksy is the anonymous British street artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Banksy's stencilled graffiti is sprayed from aerosol tins, so the spray can is his signature tool.

clue.text: Love cycling jersey's finishing in blue

indicators.note: cycling means going round in a loop, so a letter moves from one end of the word to the other

parts.note: your heart is your love, as in sweetheart

indicators.note: finishing points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cyclist loves finishing a race in a blue jersey.
explanation.walkthrough: HEART moves its first letter to the end. 'Blue' is not a colour but means smutty or risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is coarse and frank, just as a blue joke is rude or bawdy.

clue.text: Regularly whack them around and make an impression

indicators.note: turned around means facing the other way, so the kept letters are read backwards
regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is kept

parts.note: the even-placed letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Hit them repeatedly and you will leave a mark.
explanation.definitionFit: To etch is to cut lines into a surface, literally leaving an impression in metal or glass.

clue.text: 8 wood?

parts.note: surface reading: an eight-wood, a golf club
setter's reading: timber whose name is a sum that multiplies out to eight

explanation.walkthrough: Golfers carry numbered woods, so '8 wood' looks like a club; but 2 times 4 is 8, and a two-by-four is a standard length of sawn timber measuring two inches by four.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-by-four is a common piece of construction lumber, named for its cross-section in inches.

clue.text: Peak tourist period working away in open ocean

indicators.note: something taken away is removed, so those letters vanish from the phrase

parts.note: the busiest time of year for holidays
on means working or operating, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: During the busiest holiday weeks, someone is working away out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The high seas are the open waters beyond any nation's coastal limits, far from land.

clue.text: Choosy lad managed to make time for lessons?

indicators.note: managed means handled and organised, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fussy boy somehow found time to go to his lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: A school day is a weekday when pupils attend classes, the time set aside for teaching.

clue.text: Focus of whip before a Whitehall journalist took over

indicators.note: the focus of something is its centre, so the middle letters are kept

parts.note: the two central letters of the word
Jack Whitehall is an English comedian
ED is short for editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A government whip and a Whitehall reporter seem to be plotting a takeover.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall here is not the street of government offices in London but the comedian Jack Whitehall, so 'a Whitehall' is someone with his first name.
explanation.definitionFit: To hijack is to seize control of a vehicle or event, so hijacked means took over by force.

clue.text: Unemotional sort after golf clubs given away as fairground prize?

indicators.note: given away means handed over, so one letter is surrendered to make room for another

parts.note: a cold fish is an aloof, unfeeling person
Golf is the radio code word for G
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: A dour golfer, having given his clubs away, is himself a fairground prize.
explanation.walkthrough: In COLD FISH the C is given away and replaced, after it, by the G.
explanation.definitionFit: A goldfish in a plastic bag is the traditional prize for winning a game at a British funfair.

clue.text: Detest tablet on pillbox?

indicators.note: one thing set on another comes after it in the reading, so the tablet's letter follows the hat's

parts.note: a pillbox is a small round brimless hat
E is slang for an ecstasy tablet

explanation.surface: A pill placed on a pillbox looks like one you would hate to take.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pillbox' reads as a medicine container, but it is a hat; the tablet follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: To hate and to detest are synonyms, both meaning to feel intense dislike.

clue.text: Chance of alcoholic drinking a shiraz at the end

indicators.note: something drinking takes another thing into itself

parts.note: hard drinks are alcoholic ones, like spirits
taken as written

indicators.note: at the end points to the closing letter of the word

parts.note: last letter of the wine

explanation.surface: What are the odds of a heavy drinker finishing off a bottle of red wine?
explanation.definitionFit: Hazard means chance or luck, as in the old dice game and the phrase at hazard.

clue.text: This writer's work initially incites angry viewer's complaint

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself: my
OP is short for opus, a work

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each word that follows

parts.note: first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: An author's new work stirs up a furious reader's complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'viewer's complaint' is not a grumble to a broadcaster but an eye condition.
explanation.definitionFit: Myopia is short-sightedness, a disorder of vision that afflicts anyone looking at things.

clue.text: Flat/apt

definitions.meaning: second meaning: inclined or liable to

explanation.walkthrough: The slash invites reading it as a property listing, flat or apartment; instead each word is a separate meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means stretched out face down, and also tending to, as in prone to accidents.

clue.text: Once again takes on study before new post

parts.note: to read a subject is to study it at university

indicators.note: making something new means remaking it, so the letters take a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A graduate takes up research again before starting a new job.
explanation.definitionFit: To readopt is to adopt or embrace something a second time, taking it on anew.

clue.text: Fly circling round fizzy drink

indicators.note: circling means going back round, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a gnat is a small fly
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An insect buzzes round a glass of fizzy pop.
explanation.walkthrough: Tango is a British brand of orange fizzy drink. 'Round' looks like part of the insect's flight path but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Tango is a brand of carbonated soft drink, so it is an example of a fizzy drink.

clue.text: Sign record with love

parts.note: a log is a written record
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Sign the register affectionately, perhaps with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is an emblem or symbol identifying a company, a sign in the sense of a mark.

clue.text: London attraction seen in Ken Loach film about western plot

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the film's title wraps round the other letters

parts.note: Kes is Ken Loach's 1969 film about a boy and his kestrel
W is the abbreviation for western
a plot of land, such as a garden

explanation.surface: A London landmark features in a Ken Loach film about a Wild West land dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' tempts as a story line, but it is a piece of ground. Kew Gardens is the Royal Botanic Gardens in south-west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Kew Gardens is a famous botanic garden and tourist site in London, so it is an example of a London attraction.

clue.text: Father and I ultimately lie in bed all day to get warm

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title
taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so the last letter of each word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Dad and I stay under the duvet all day to keep cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Warm' reads as heat, but it describes a cordial manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A warm welcome is a friendly one, so warm and friendly are synonyms for a kindly manner.

clue.text: Problem for 14 year old with temperature seeing doctor first

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviation for doctor
yr is the abbreviation for year
O is the abbreviation for old
T is the symbol for temperature

explanation.surface: A fourteen-year-old with a fever sees the doctor before anything else.
explanation.walkthrough: '14' reads as an age, but it points to the answer at 14 down, a length of timber; 'doctor first' puts that abbreviation at the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Dry rot is a fungal decay that crumbles timber, so it is a threat to a wooden beam.
